content.value_statement: Abrupt transitions, repetition, and awkward sentences can make short video scripts difficult to follow. This skill identifies specific weaknesses and suggests conversational revisions while preserving your original text.
actual_capabilities: Divide scripts into numbered paragraphs with topic summaries and narrative roles.
Identify missing connections between adjacent paragraphs and suggest transitions or reordered sections.
Flag repetition, redundant examples, and low-information passages.
Suggest shorter sentences, plain-language explanations, and more natural spoken phrasing.
Prioritize script issues by potential viewer disengagement and quote the affected passages.
Provide requested revisions with visible deletion, addition, and restoration markers plus a change-summary table.
limitations: Viewer disengagement ratings are editorial judgments, not measured retention statistics or guaranteed performance predictions.
The review concerns expression and structure, not factual verification or changing arguments, examples, or data.
Results appear as Markdown in the conversation; the skill does not create, save, or open local review files.
Suggestions involving whiteboards, gestures, or visual cues may require clarification of the filming format.

use_cases.title: Review a creator script before recording
use_cases.description: Locate abrupt transitions and difficult sentences, then prioritize changes before recording a short video.

use_cases.title: Document editorial feedback for collaborators
use_cases.description: Produce paragraph-level findings and annotated revisions while retaining the original wording for comparison.

use_cases.title: Clarify spoken lessons
use_cases.description: Check whether terminology, supporting examples, and paragraph order help learners follow an explanation without removing necessary teaching context.

prompt_templates.title: Check a script
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this short video script for logical transitions, repetition, and spoken flow. Quote each issue and prioritize the risks. Script: [paste script]

prompt_templates.title: Repair paragraph connections
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this script for missing connections between paragraphs. Suggest brief transitions while preserving my arguments and tone. Script: [paste script]

prompt_templates.title: Revise with visible changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review and revise this script with visible deletion and addition markers. Preserve my original text, tone, and claims. Include a change-summary table. Script: [paste script]
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with explicit revision permission

prompt_templates.title: Review a visually supported explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review and annotate this whiteboard script. Preserve visual cues and necessary explanations. Prioritize logical gaps and redundancy. Ask before edits requiring missing filming details. Script: [paste script]

output_examples.input: Review this transition: The team missed its deadline. We should reduce meeting frequency.
output: Priority: High. The second sentence proposes a solution without explaining why meetings caused the delay.
Suggested transition: Frequent status meetings reduced the time available to finish the work.
Use this transition only if it accurately reflects the situation.

output_examples.input: Check spoken flow: In light of the circumstances described above, it is necessary for us to undertake a comprehensive evaluation.
output: Priority: Minor suggestion. The sentence uses formal phrasing that may sound unnatural when spoken.
Suggested wording: We need to review what happened.
Keep any details that the surrounding explanation requires.

output_examples.input: Check this whiteboard script for repetition: First, set a goal. Look here. Next, choose one action.
output: The phrase Look here may direct attention to the whiteboard and should remain if it supports a visual cue.
The sequence from goal to action is clear.

best_practices: Provide the complete script and any filming details that affect gestures, lists, or visual references.
Specify whether you want a review only or annotated revisions.
Review high-priority transitions first, then read proposed changes aloud to confirm they match your voice.
anti_patterns: Treating editorial risk labels as measured completion rates or guaranteed audience outcomes.
Removing examples or visual cues solely because they appear repetitive without considering their explanatory role.
Requesting factual validation or expecting the skill to save and open review files.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews paragraph connections, information density, and spoken delivery in short video scripts.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my script automatically?
faq.answer: It revises only when you request changes in the current conversation or an earlier message. A review-only request remains a review.

faq.question: Does it preserve my original wording?
faq.answer: Requested revisions retain the original text with visible change markers and a change-summary table.

faq.question: Can it predict actual viewer retention?
faq.answer: No. It identifies possible disengagement points through editorial review, without measuring audience behavior or guaranteeing results.

faq.question: Does it support scripts with visual aids?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers whiteboards, gestures, and visual cues, and requests filming details when they affect an edit.

faq.question: Does it create files or require a specific notes application?
faq.answer: No. It delivers ordinary Markdown in the conversation and does not create, save, or open local review files.
